title: Nvidia RTX Spark Laptops Go On Sale From $2,599 For Local AI
excerpt: The Blackwell-and-Grace superchip machines from six PC makers promise frontier models and agents on the device, even as chip shares stay under pressure.
body:
• Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops went on sale worldwide on October 16 from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599.
  • The single superchip pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with a Grace CPU co-designed with MediaTek, with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance.
  • The pitch is local AI: large models and agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw run on the laptop itself, without sending every task to the cloud.
  • Before buying, check the memory configuration — the $2,599 entry models carry far less than the 128GB ceiling, and independent reviews are only just appearing.

Nvidia's first Windows laptops built around its own chip went on sale around the world on Friday, October 16, as the company opened a new retail channel for local artificial intelligence: premium machines, starting at $2,599, designed to run large AI models and personal agents on the device rather than in a data centre. The launch, detailed in Nvidia's official announcement, brings systems from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI to stores and manufacturers' websites globally.

The product news landed in a difficult week for chip shares. Nvidia's stock has been under pressure along with the wider semiconductor sector, sliding in recent sessions as investors questioned the debt funding the AI data-centre build-out — a backdrop that left the shares lower even as the company's newest hardware reached customers. The contrast underlines the two stories running through Nvidia at once: booming product ambition, and a market newly sensitive to how the AI boom is financed.

One chip, one pool of memory

RTX Spark is a single superchip combining a Blackwell RTX graphics processor with a Grace central processor, an Arm-based design developed with MediaTek, according to launch-day coverage of the machines. Its defining feature is memory: up to 128GB shared between the CPU and GPU in one pool. On a conventional laptop the graphics chip holds only a small slice of memory of its own, which limits the size of AI model that can run locally. A large shared pool removes that bottleneck.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=_tsiWjmWEZ8

Nvidia rates the platform at up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance and says it can run frontier models locally, render 3D scenes larger than 90GB, edit 8K 4:2:2 video and play AAA games at 1440p at more than 100 frames per second. Those are the manufacturer's figures; independent testing is only beginning, and buyers should treat them as claims to be verified rather than settled results.

Agents out of the box

The software story is agents. Nvidia says guided installers let owners set up tools including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy without using a command line, and it is shipping its own Nemotron 3.5 Bolt model — a 74-billion-parameter model tuned for tool calling and multi-step tasks — for supported configurations. Its OpenShell secure runtime and Microsoft Execution Containers are meant to control what an agent may access on the machine, and a feature called Nvidia PAIR lets an RTX Spark laptop serve AI inference to other Windows, Linux and Mac computers on a home network.

For developers, Nvidia and Microsoft have prepared the first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm, a native Python and Conda installer, and support covering 97% of the top 15,000 Python packages. Adobe is offering beta versions of Photoshop and Premiere with native support at launch. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and chief executive, described the machines as a new generation of Windows PC built for today's work and for the personal AI agents people will work with next.

What the $2,599 buys — and what it does not

The starting price buys the entry configuration, not the headline specification. The launch line-up spans the ASUS ProArt P14 and P16, Dell XPS 16, HP OmniBook Ultra and OmniBook X 14, Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n, Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra and MSI's Prestige N16 models, and prices climb steeply with memory — top configurations cost several times the entry price. Nvidia has not published a single price list across models and countries, so the memory and storage on any specific machine need checking before purchase.

Why it matters

RTX Spark is Nvidia's most direct move yet to shift AI computing from rented cloud capacity to hardware customers own outright, and it gives Windows buyers an alternative to Apple's unified-memory Macs, which have become a popular way to run large models at home. Whether the premium is worth paying depends on how well local agents perform in daily use — the question reviews in the coming weeks will answer. Nvidia says additional systems, including compact desktops, will follow.
